name: Doxel lidar scanning robot
summary: A tracked robot with a laser scanner that Doxel used from 2018 to scan building sites after hours and compare installed work with the model; Doxel now captures sites with hard-hat 360° cameras instead.

germany.statusNote: No longer offered: Doxel's current site describes capture only with 360° cameras worn on a hard hat (Insta360 models) or drone footage and has no robot page. The robot was never sold; Doxel used it itself to scan customer sites (2018).

specs.label: Time to scan a building
specs.conditions: entire multi-floor medical office building in San Diego, scanned daily (2018 report)

specs.label: Stairs
specs.conditions: prescheduled scan paths can include stairs

notes: Discontinued: Doxel now offers only its software service with hard-hat 360° cameras or drone footage.
Drove autonomously along prescheduled paths after the site closed; the data went to Doxel's cloud for deep-learning object recognition.
Tracked base with flippers carrying a laser scanner (maker photo); the 2018 report says Doxel's work was mostly indoors.

evidence.task: Scanned a multi-floor medical office building every day (4.5 h per scan) to track installed work against the plan; Doxel reports 38% higher labour productivity and the project 11% under budget
evidence.where: Medical office building, San Diego, USA
evidence.note: Doxel case study as reported by IEEE Spectrum; customer not named.
